# Exactly 3 rows × 5 columns (15 buttons total)
ROWS = [
    [("pBtn", "P", "P"), ("qBtn", "Q", "Q"), ("rBtn", "R", "R"), ("sBtn", "S", "S"), ("tBtn", "T", "T")],
    [("andBtn", "∧", " ∧ "), ("orBtn", "∨", " ∨ "), ("negBtn", "¬", "¬"), ("impliesBtn", "⇒", " ⇒ "), ("iffBtn", "⇔", " ⇔ ")],
    [("lbracketBtn", "(", "("), ("rbracketBtn", ")", ")"), ("enterBtn", "⏎", "\n"), ("backspaceBtn", "⌫", ""), ("runBtn", "RUN", "")]
]

OPERATOR_CHUNKS = (" ∧ ", " ∨ ", " ⇒ ", " ⇔ ")

# Input Section containing Array1 and Radio Buttons side-by-side
with ui.div(cls="input-section-card"):
    ui.div("Input Section", cls="input-section-title")
    with ui.div(cls="input-top-layout"):
        with ui.div(cls="pad-container"):
            for row in ROWS:
                with ui.div(cls="button-row"):
                    for btn_id, label, _ in row:
                        ui.input_action_button(btn_id, label)
        
        with ui.div(cls="radio-container"):
            ui.input_radio_buttons(
                "analysis_mode",
                "Select Analysis Type:",
                choices=[
                    "Check Premises Consistency",
                    "Check Argument Validity",
                    "Calculate System Reliability",
                    "Calculate Top Event Probability"
                ],
                selected="Check Premises Consistency"
            )

# Text Area Section
with ui.div(cls="text-container"):
    ui.input_text_area(
        "formula_input",
        label="Logical Formula / Premises (one per line):",
        value="",
        rows=8,
        cols=80,
        width="100%",
        placeholder="Click buttons from Array1 or type your formula...",
    )

formula_val = reactive.Value("")

def make_handler(btn_id: str, text: str):
    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input[btn_id])
    def _():
        formula_val.set(formula_val.get() + text)

for row in ROWS:
    for btn_id, _, text in row:
        if text:
            make_handler(btn_id, text)

@reactive.effect
@reactive.event(input.backspaceBtn)
def handle_backspace():
    current = formula_val.get()
    for op in OPERATOR_CHUNKS:
        if current.endswith(op):
            formula_val.set(current[: -len(op)])
            return
    formula_val.set(current[:-1])

run_trigger = reactive.Value(0)

@reactive.effect
@reactive.event(input.runBtn)
def handle_run():
    run_trigger.set(run_trigger.get() + 1)

@reactive.effect
def update_textarea():
    ui.update_text_area("formula_input", value=formula_val.get())

@reactive.effect
@reactive.event(input.formula_input)
def sync_manual_typing():
    formula_val.set(input.formula_input())

@reactive.calc
def lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in formula_val.get().split("\n") if ln.strip()]

@reactive.calc
def active_vars():
    lns = lines()
    if not lns:
        return []
    listed = ["P", "Q", "R", "S", "T"]
    found = []
    for var in listed:
        if any(var in ln for ln in lns):
            found.append(var)
    return found

# Dynamic Parameters Section for Reliability / Probability Modes
with ui.div(cls="output-section"):
    ui.h4("Parameters & Configuration")
    @render.ui
    def show_parameters():
        mode = input.analysis_mode()
        vars_list = active_vars()
        
        if mode in ["Calculate System Reliability", "Calculate Top Event Probability"]:
            if not vars_list:
                return ui.p("Please enter a valid formula containing variables (P, Q, R, S, T) to configure parameters.")
            
            inputs_ui = []
            label_prefix = "Component Reliability" if mode == "Calculate System Reliability" else "Basic Event Probability"
            for v in vars_list:
                default_val = 0.9 if mode == "Calculate System Reliability" else 0.1
                inputs_ui.append(
                    ui.input_numeric(f"param_{v}", f"{label_prefix} for {v}:", value=default_val, min=0.0, max=1.0, step=0.05)
                )
            return ui.div(cls="parameter-section", *inputs_ui)
        return ui.p("No additional parameters required for this analysis mode.")

# Text area lines representation
with ui.div(cls="lines-output"):
    @render.code
    def show_lines():
        return repr(lines())

# Analysis Results Section (Triggered ONLY on RUN click)
with ui.div(cls="output-section"):
    ui.h4("Analysis Results")
    
    @render.ui
    def show_results():
        # Takes reactive dependency ONLY on run_trigger (the RUN button)
        _ = run_trigger.get() 
        
        # Isolate inputs so typing, mode changing, or parameter sliding don't trigger auto-calculation
        with reactive.isolate():
            mode = input.analysis_mode()
            lns = lines()
            
            if not lns:
                return ui.div(
                    ui.p(ui.strong("Selected Analysis Mode: "), mode),
                    ui.p("Status: Please enter at least one formula or premise and click 'RUN'.", style="color: red;")
                )
            
            try:
                # Initialize variables and evaluate via core.py
                core.init_vars(lns)
                
                results_elements = [
                    ui.p(ui.strong("Selected Analysis Mode: "), mode),
                    ui.p(ui.strong("Active Formula Lines: "), str(len(lns)))
                ]
                
                # 1. Premises Consistency
                if mode == "Check Premises Consistency":
                    consistent, row_num = core.check_consistency(lns)
                    if consistent:
                        results_elements.append(ui.p(ui.strong("Result: "), "The premises are CONSISTENT.", style="color: green; font-weight: bold;"))
                    else:
                        results_elements.append(ui.p(ui.strong("Result: "), f"The premises are INCONSISTENT (conflict at row {row_num}).", style="color: red; font-weight: bold;"))
                
                # 2. Argument Validity
                elif mode == "Check Argument Validity":
                    if len(lns) < 2:
                        results_elements.append(ui.p("Error: Argument validity check requires at least 2 lines (premises followed by conclusion on the last line).", style="color: red;"))
                    else:
                        valid, row_num = core.check_argument_validity(lns)
                        if valid:
                            results_elements.append(ui.p(ui.strong("Result: "), "The argument is VALID.", style="color: green; font-weight: bold;"))
                        else:
                            results_elements.append(ui.p(ui.strong("Result: "), f"The argument is INVALID (counterexample at row {row_num}).", style="color: red; font-weight: bold;"))
                
                # 3. System Reliability
                elif mode == "Calculate System Reliability":
                    if len(lns) > 1:
                        results_elements.append(ui.p("Note: Reliability calculation uses the first formula line as the system expression.", style="color: orange;"))
                    sys_expr = lns[0]
                    vars_list = active_vars()
                    reliabilities = {}
                    for v in vars_list:
                        val = input.get(f"param_{v}", 0.9)
                        reliabilities[v] = float(val) if val is not None else 0.9
                    
                    rel = core.calculate_reliability(sys_expr, reliabilities)
                    results_elements.append(ui.p(ui.strong("System Reliability: "), f"{rel:.6f} ({rel * 100:.2f}%)", style="color: blue; font-weight: bold;"))
                
                # 4. Top Event Probability
                elif mode == "Calculate Top Event Probability":
                    if len(lns) > 1:
                        results_elements.append(ui.p("Note: Top event probability uses the first formula line as the top event expression.", style="color: orange;"))
                    top_expr = lns[0]
                    vars_list = active_vars()
                    probabilities = {}
                    for v in vars_list:
                        val = input.get(f"param_{v}", 0.1)
                        probabilities[v] = float(val) if val is not None else 0.1
                    
                    prob = core.calculate_top_event_probability(top_expr, probabilities)
                    results_elements.append(ui.p(ui.strong("Top Event Probability: "), f"{prob:.6f} ({prob * 100:.2f}%)", style="color: blue; font-weight: bold;"))

                # Include PDNF and PCNF for single statements
                if len(lns) == 1:
                    stmt = lns[0]
                    pdnf = core.generate_pdnf(stmt)
                    pcnf = core.generate_pcnf(stmt)
                    results_elements.extend([
                        ui.hr(),
                        ui.p(ui.strong("PDNF (Principal Disjunctive Normal Form): "), pdnf),
                        ui.p(ui.strong("PCNF (Principal Conjunctive Normal Form): "), pcnf)
                    ])
                
                # Generate and Render Truth Table
                tt = core.gen_truth_table()
                if tt:
                    headers = list(tt.keys())
                    num_rows = len(list(tt.values())[0])
                    
                    table_headers = [ui.tags.th(h) for h in headers]
                    table_rows = []
                    for r_idx in range(num_rows):
                        row_cells = [ui.tags.td(tt[h][r_idx]) for h in headers]
                        table_rows.append(ui.tags.tr(*row_cells))
                    
                    results_elements.extend([
                        ui.hr(),
                        ui.h5("Truth Table"),
                        ui.tags.table(
                            ui.tags.thead(ui.tags.tr(*table_headers)),
                            ui.tags.tbody(*table_rows),
                            cls="truth-table"
                        )
                    ])

                return ui.div(*results_elements)

            except Exception as e:
                return ui.div(
                    ui.p(ui.strong("Selected Analysis Mode: "), mode),
                    ui.p(f"Error executing analysis: {str(e)}", style="color: red; font-weight: bold;")
                )

# GLOBAL LOOKUP TABLES =========================================================
CONN = {
    "∧": "_and",
    "∨": "_or",
    "⇒": "_implies",
    "⇔": "_iff"
}

EXPR = {}

USED_VARS = []
# ==============================================================================

# MY FUNCTIONS ====================================================================
def _implies(var1: str, var2: str) -> str:
    if len(var1) != len(var2): raise Exception("Size of both variables must be the same!")

    out = ""
    for idx in range(len(var1)):
        if (var1[idx] == "1") and (var2[idx] == "0"): out += "0"
        else: out += "1"
    return out


def _iff(var1: str, var2: str) -> str:
    if len(var1) != len(var2): raise Exception("Size of both variables must be the same!")

    out = ""
    for idx in range(len(var1)):
        if var1[idx] == var2[idx]: out += "1"
        else: out += "0"
    return out


def translate(expr: str) -> str:
    expr = expr.strip()

    # Base Case: Single Variable
    if expr.isalpha() and len(expr) == 1:
        return EXPR[expr]
    
    # Removes outer parantheses if it encloses the whole statement
    if expr.startswith("(") and expr.endswith(")"):
        depth = 0
        encloses_all = True
        
        for i, char in enumerate(expr):
            if char == "(": depth += 1
            elif char == ")": depth -= 1

            if depth == 0 and i < len(expr) - 1: 
                encloses_all = False
                break
        
        if encloses_all:
            expr = expr[1:-1].strip()

    # Find the top-level connector
    depth = 0
    for i, char in enumerate(expr):
        if char == "(": depth += 1
        elif char == ")": depth -= 1

        elif depth == 0 and char in CONN:
            left_operand = expr[:i].strip()
            right_operand = expr[i+1:].strip()

            if not left_operand: raise ValueError("Missing left operand")
            if not right_operand: raise ValueError("Missing right operand")
            
            function = CONN[char]

            return f"{function}(str({translate(left_operand)}), str({translate(right_operand)}))"
    # Handle Negation
    if expr.startswith("¬"):
        operand = expr[1:].strip()
        
        if not operand: raise ValueError("Missing operand after negation")

        return f"_not(str({translate(operand)}))"

    raise ValueError(f"Invalid Expression: {expr}")


def check_argument_validity(statements: list[str]) -> tuple[bool, (int | None)]:
    conclusion = EXPR[statements[-1]]
    num_rows = len(conclusion)
    for row in range(num_rows):
        all_premises_true = all([EXPR[premise][row] == "1" for premise in statements[:-1]])
        if all_premises_true and conclusion[row] == "0": return False, (row + 1)

    return True, None


def check_consistency(premises: list[str]) -> tuple[bool, (int | None)]:
    num_rows = len(EXPR[premises[0]])

    for row in range(num_rows):
        all_premises_true = all([EXPR[premise][row] == "1" for premise in premises])
        if all_premises_true: return True, None

    return False, (row + 1)


def calculate_reliability(statement: str, comp_reliabilities: dict[str, float]) -> float:
    system = EXPR[statement]
    num_rows = len(system)
    reliability = 0.0

    for row in range(num_rows):
        if system[row] == "1":
            row_probability = 1.0

            for var in USED_VARS:
                comp_reliability = comp_reliabilities[var]

                if EXPR[var][row] == "1": row_probability *= comp_reliability
                else: row_probability *= 1 - comp_reliability
            
            reliability += row_probability
    
    return reliability


def calculate_top_event_probability(statement: str, basic_event_probabilities: dict[str, float]) -> float:
    top_event = EXPR[statement]
    num_rows = len(top_event)
    probability = 0.0

    for row in range(num_rows):
        if top_event[row] == "1":
            row_probability = 1.0

            for var in USED_VARS:
                basic_event_probability = basic_event_probabilities[var]

                if EXPR[var][row] == "0": row_probability *= basic_event_probability
                else: row_probability *= 1 - basic_event_probability

            probability += row_probability
        
    return probability


def generate_pdnf(statement: list[str]) -> str:
    results = EXPR[statement[0]]
    num_rows = len(results)
    min_terms = []

    for row in range(num_rows):
        if results[row] == "1":
            literals = []

            for var in USED_VARS:
                if EXPR[var][row] == "1": literals.append(var)
                else: literals.append("¬" + var)

            min_terms.append("(" + " ∧ ".join(literals) + ")")

    if not min_terms:
        return "The proposition is a Fallacy"
    
    return " ∨ ".join(min_terms)


def generate_pcnf(statement: list[str]) -> str:
    results = EXPR[statement[0]]
    num_rows = len(results)
    max_terms = []

    for row in range(num_rows):
        if results[row] == "0":
            literals = []

            for var in USED_VARS:
                if EXPR[var][row] == "0": literals.append(var)
                else: literals.append("¬" + var)
            
            max_terms.append("(" + " ∨ ".join(literals) + ")")

    if not max_terms:
        return "The proposition is a Totality"

    return " ∧ ".join(max_terms)


def gen_truth_table() -> dict[str, str]:
    truth_table = {}
    conversion = {"1": "T", "0": "F"}

    for key, value in EXPR.items():
        truth_table[key] = [conversion[i] for i in value]

    return truth_table
# ==============================================================================

# GLOBAL LOOKUP TABLES =========================================================
# ==============================================================================

# MY FUNCTIONS =================================================================
def init_vars(statements: list[str]) -> None:
    """
    ARGUMENTS:
        statements: list[str]
            User input from the UI.
    
    Adds variables to the EXPR dictionary.
    """
    listed_variables = ["P", "Q", "R", "S", "T"]
    used_variables = []

    for var in listed_variables:
        for statement in statements:
            if var in statement:
                used_variables.append(var)
                break
    
    num_vars = len(used_variables)
    for idx, var in enumerate(used_variables):
        num_subsections = 2**(idx+1)        # No of subsections of the representation
        subsection_length = 2**(num_vars - idx - 1)    # Length of each individual subsection
        variable = ""                   
        flag = 1
        for j in range(num_subsections):
            variable += f"{flag}"*subsection_length
            if flag == 1: flag = 0
            else: flag = 1
        EXPR[var] = variable

    for statement in statements:
        EXPR[statement] = str(eval(translate(statement)))
    
    return None

def _and(var1: str, var2: str) -> str:
    """AND operator for two variables of same length."""
    if len(var1) != len(var2): raise Exception("Size of both variables must be the same!")

    out = ""
    for idx in range(len(var1)):
        if (var1[idx] == "1") and (var2[idx] == "1"): out += "1"
        else: out += "0"
    return out

def _or(var1: str, var2: str) -> str:
    """OR operator for two variables of same length."""
    if len(var1) != len(var2): raise Exception("Size of both variables must be the same!")

    out = ""
    for idx in range(len(var1)):
        if (var1[idx] == "0") and (var2[idx] == "0"): out += "0"
        else: out += "1"
    return out

def _not(var1: str) -> str:
    """NOT operator for a variable."""
    out = ""
    for idx in range(len(var1)):
        if var1[idx] == "0": out+= "1"
        else: out += "0"
    return out
